title: Proportionality and Risk-Based Prioritisation
summary: How to match supervisory effort and response to the size of the risk, prioritise issues across a portfolio, and select the right tool from the supervisory toolkit.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to match supervisory effort and response to the size of the risk, prioritise issues across a portfolio, and select the right tool from the supervisory toolkit.
Learning Objectives: Apply proportionality to the scale, nature and impact of a firm's risks
Prioritise issues using impact, probability and supervisory objectives
Select a supervisory tool or intervention that fits the risk
Syllabus: Proportionality in principle and in practice
Impact and probability: prioritising across firms and issues
The supervisory toolkit: from dialogue to formal powers
Avoiding both regulatory overreach and supervisory forbearance
Intended Audience: Supervisors and senior supervisors responsible for risk assessments, firm engagement and supervisory findings
Team leaders and managers who review, challenge and sign off supervisory judgements and correspondence
Staff in enforcement, authorisation and policy functions who rely on, or contribute to, supervisory conclusions
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervising regulated firms is helpful. The programme is suitable for both newer and experienced supervisors.
Core Reading: IMF, The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08, 2010)
IMF, Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181, 2023)
Daniel Kahneman, Olivier Sibony and Cass R. Sunstein, Noise: A Flaw in Human Judgment (2021)
Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011)
